Primary pain: per-user cost too high at current token rates. CTO Alberto: 'Users send large system prompts + repeated context across turns, and we can't afford that per request.' Wants quick wins: batching for bulk background tasks, prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts, prompt compression/templating to cut tokens.

Customer-provided artifacts: sample traffic CSV (tokens/day estimate) + 10 example chat transcripts. SE notes: ~40% of tokens are repeated system instructions; many short messages could be batched for background embedding/reranking workloads.

Quoted asks from call: 'Can you run a token audit and propose concrete token-savings? What batching/caching params should we flip in hosted API? Any SDK/guide we can ship to devs?'

Potential fit: hosted_api self-serve + Redwood Optimize recommendations. Low friction pilot: token audit + 2-week POC demonstrating 30-40% token reduction using prompt compression + prefix cache.

Risks/blockers: SOC2 confirmation required by a handful of early customers; needs a simple contract/FAQ for audit/compliance. Budget: tight; likely monthly usage-based plan under $2k/month initially.
